extracted.intended_audience: NSF program officers, program directors, peer reviewers, and principal investigators
extracted.subtask_description: Official National Science Foundation / National Science Board policy and resolution describing required peer review procedures for NSF grant proposals, including exceptions, reviewer selection, confidentiality, disclosure to PIs, reporting, and the primary evaluation criteria reviewers should apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Once reconsideration by the Deputy Director has been completed, no further reconsideration will be made of the proposal or of a substantively identical proposal submitted thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not preclude the submission of a substantially revised proposal in the same program area for consideration as a new proposal under the usual review and evaluation procedures. If more time is necessary, the requestor will be notified in writing of the reasons therefor and of the date by which the written report is expected to be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for external peer review (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the National Science Foundation that the evaluation of all formal proposals for NSF funding includes external peer review with the following exceptions: proposals submitted in response to formal solicitations governed by the Federal Procurement Regulations; proposals to provide goods or services normally obtained through purchase orders or requisitions; other proposals for which peer review has been waived by the Director or his designee; and proposals which are withdrawn prior to decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A report on the use of the waiver category must be included in the Director's periodic report to the Board. Some classes of proposals may be excepted categorically (examples noted: travel grants, committed renewals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary method of peer review must be selected and announced
rubrics_metrics.description: Each program shall select one primary method for peer review which will represent the minimum review received by proposals in that program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review generally takes the form of ad hoc or mail reviews; reviews by an assembled panel of peers; or a combination of the two. The primary method can be supplemented with additional reviews, site visits, etc., as needed for individual proposals or activities. After approval by the Director or his designee, the primary method of peer review in each program, including the evaluation criteria reviewers are requested to consider, shall be suitably announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria — representation and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of reviewers shall be made in accordance with criteria established to accomplish the objective of full and fair consideration. Factors to be considered in the selection of reviewers include an appropriate representation of relevant skills, viewpoints, and backgrounds needed to evaluate each proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent practical, reviewers should be selected to obtain a wide representation of reviewers in terms of geographic distribution, type of institution represented, race and sex of reviewers, etc. Program officers should seek broadly representative participation of qualified individuals as reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of reviews and reviewer identities
rubrics_metrics.description: In no case is a review to be associated with an individual panel member, a reviewer (panel or ad hoc), or subgroup of an entire panel, except as required by law. Names of ad hoc reviewers are confidential and are not to be released except as required by law or as provided in related policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy stresses that reviewer identities generally remain confidential; however, related resolutions indicate the Foundation will publish annually a list of all reviewers used by each division and office (see reporting obligations). The question of including the identity of the reviewer with verbatim reviews will be considered further by the National Science Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability to principal investigators of review materials and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal investigators shall be informed by the Foundation of the availability upon request of: (A) verbatim, unsigned copies of all peer reviews; (B) the criteria established for the review; and (C) a summary of the Foundation's reasons for its decision on the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resolution specifies that verbatim copies of reviews requested by the Foundation after January 1, 1976 (not including the identity of the reviewer) will be made available to the PI/PD upon request; reviews requested prior to that date remain governed by earlier policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer evaluation criteria (primary review factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The main criteria reviewers should apply are: (1) the significance of the scientific investigation described in the proposal; (2) the ability of the applicant to carry out the proposed research; and (3) the capacity of the applicant institution to support the type of research in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where all these factors are roughly equal, another set of criteria (including geographic location of the applicant's institution) may be considered. Heavy emphasis is placed on the quality of the work described in the proposal and on the past research performance of the applicant. Reviewers are asked to rate proposals as excellent, very good, good, fair or poor and to present written comments supporting their ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory nature of reviews and program director responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews by mail reviewers or panel members are advisory and the program director has the final responsibility for deciding whether or not a proposal is to be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although advisory, peer-review ratings are an important source of information and advice and program directors typically rely heavily on reviewers' evaluations in funding decisions. The policy recognizes a need to balance fairness, openness, and efficiency, and documents and reporting are required to provide oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's annual reporting obligations on peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall provide the Board no less than annually a report on the Foundation's use of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The annual report shall include: a published list, by Division, of all reviewers used during the preceding year; information on the waiver of peer review for proposals under the exceptions; statistical analyses of the use of peer review; recommendations for change or further consideration of the Foundation's policies on peer review; and such other information as the Director may feel appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when review timing is delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: If more time is necessary, the requestor will be notified in writing of the reasons therefor and of the date by which the written report is expected to be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to requests for reconsideration and other instances where completion of review or reconsideration is delayed.
